decision.explanation: Set f(x)=0: -5\sqrt[4]{3x+1}+10=0, so \sqrt[4]{3x+1}=2. Raising both sides to the fourth power gives 3x+1=16, hence x=5.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
To find the root of $f(x),$  we must solve $f(x)=0:$

$$
-5\sqrt[4]{3x+1}+10=0
$$

We solve this equation by making $x$ the subject, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-5\sqrt[4]{3x+1}+10 & =0 \\ -5\sqrt[4]{3x+1} & =-10 \\ \sqrt[4]{3x+1} & =2 \\ (\sqrt[4]{3x+1})^{4} & ={2}^{4} \\ 3x+1 & =16 \\ 3x & =15 \\ x & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we must check the answer by substituting it back into the initial equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}-5\sqrt[4]{3\cdot 5+1}+10 & =0 \\ -5\sqrt[4]{16}+10 & =0 \\ -5\cdot 2+10 & =0 \\ 0 & =0\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the root of $f(x)$ is $x=5.$

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
To find the root of $f(x),$ we must solve $f(x)=0:$

$$
2\sqrt[5]{7-6x}+6=0
$$

We solve this equation by making $x$ the subject, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\sqrt[5]{7-6x}+6 & =0 \\ 2\sqrt[5]{7-6x} & =-6 \\ \sqrt[5]{7-6x} & =-3 \\ (\sqrt[5]{7-6x})^{5} & =(-3)^{5} \\ 7-6x & =-243 \\ -6x & =-250 \\ x & =\frac{125}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the root of $f(x)$ is $x=\frac{125}{3}.$
